title: Direct age evidence for Early Middle and Late Upper Palaeolithic archaeology at Richings Park (Langley, England): Implications for the chronology of the Middle Thames
content:
ABSTRACT

Pleistocene deposits of the Middle Thames terraces and the Langley Silt Complex (LSC) contain Middle and Upper Palaeolithic archaeology. Investigation of these archaeological records and their implications for regional and North European settlement history has been limited by an absence of direct dating, mischaracterisations of the LSC, and a partial understanding of their context. Work at Richings Park has provided a new stratigraphic and chronological framework, based on absolute dates. Reassessment of the Middle and Late Upper Palaeolithic archaeology from the area illustrates that, rather than dating to late Marine Isotope Stage (MIS) 8/early MIS 7, the Early Middle Palaeolithic (EMP) archaeology probably dates to MIS 7. This challenges existing English settlement models and suggests closer correlation with northern European patterns. Additionally, the results address the mischaracterisation of the LSC as dating to MIS 2 and having minimal potential to contain archaeology; the LSC in this location comprises sediments laid down by a range of processes, from at least MIS 5c–a onwards, and contains significant, largely overlooked Late Middle and Late Upper Palaeolithic archaeology.
